entries.body: When `cargo test ... | grep/tail` hangs long after tests finish, check for leaked long-lived child processes (e.g. `sleep 300` servers spawned by tests): they inherit the test binary's stdout/stderr, hold the pipe's write end open, and the pipe reader blocks until they exit — up to the child's full lifetime per invocation. entries.body: Codex's TUI runs a paste-burst detector over UNFRAMED PTY input. Writing a payload above roughly 1 KB as one raw burst and then a bare CR makes Codex consume that CR as the paste's TERMINATOR instead of reading it as Enter. Every later message types more text into the same stuck draft. Fix: wrap the payload in explicit bracketed paste (ESC[200~ ... ESC[201~) before the trailing CR. entries.title: git log -z parsing + watermark ordering (cas-src history index)
entries.body: Three git facts verified empirically while building the cas-src structural history index (cas-7a21), each of which silently corrupts an index if assumed wrong: 1. `--name-status` and `--numstat` CANNOT be combined in one `git log` — the later flag wins and the other's data is silently absent (no error). A loop that always advances 2 misaligns every entry after a rename. numstat is `ins\tdel\tpath\0`, and `ins\tdel\t\0old\0new\0` for renames. Binary files report `-` for both counts; keep them NULL, don't coerce to 0. 3.

entries.title: Never stamp execution_note=additive-only on tasks that edit existing files
entries.body: The `additive-only` execution_note is hard-enforced at close: any M/D/R diff line fails the gate. So it must ONLY go on tasks that purely ADD new files. Do NOT put it on skill/doc/config-edit tasks (e.g. editing cas-supervisor.md or casting types in an existing .rs file), which are modifications (M lines). entries.title: Never call a failure pre-existing without baseline proof
entries.body: Never describe a compile or test failure as pre-existing, unrelated, or already present on main unless a fresh baseline run or equivalent commit-level evidence proves that classification. Until then, treat it as an introduced release blocker, diagnose it, and get the full suite green before shipping. Do not invent a known-main-failure narrative to rationalize a red integration result.

entries.title: Don't run Rust build/test gates in /tmp — it's a 32G tmpfs
entries.body: `/tmp` on this machine is tmpfs (32G, RAM-backed). A cold Rust build there exhausts it mid-compile -> "No space left on device (os error 28)" -> corrupted/partial binaries -> MASS spurious test failures (saw "678 failed" that was pure disk exhaustion, not code). The root fs (/home) has 430G. When creating a worktree for a merge/release gate (`git worktree add`), put it under /home (e.g. /home/<user>/cas-ship), NOT /tmp. If a full suite suddenly shows hundreds of failures across unrelated subsystems, suspect environment (disk/tmpfs) before code: check `df -h /tmp` and run one test with full output to see the real error.

entries.title: Slack huddle "no microphone permission" every boot — autostart vs pipewire-restart race (FIXED 2026-06-03)
entries.body: Slack huddles reported "no microphone permission" on every boot of soundwave. Root cause: ~/.config/autostart/slack.desktop launches Slack at session start; its Chromium AudioService binds PipeWire ~2s BEFORE pipewire-restart.service (the ALC897 boot-race workaround) restarts pipewire/wireplumber/pulse. entries.body: On this host (Wayland), `printf ... | wl-copy` from an agent Bash tool call reports success but the clipboard is EMPTY by the time the user pastes: wl-copy serves clipboard content from a live process, and the sandbox kills children when the tool call exits. entries.title: Respect task lock — don't race a claimed task
entries.body: When `mcp__cas__task action=start` returns a lock error (task already claimed by another agent), stop immediately. Do NOT proceed with implementation hoping to "win" — the lock means another worker is already executing the task. Racing causes duplicate work, wasted build time, and a confusing duplicate branch. The correct response is: (1) note the task is locked, (2) message the supervisor that the assignment appears double-booked, (3) wait for supervisor guidance. entries.title: Fast-follow tasks on closed epics target main directly
entries.body: When a task is a fast-follow on a closed/shipped epic, target `main` directly for the worker branch PR — do NOT merge into the epic branch. The epic branch (`epic/...`) is frozen once the epic ships to prod; merging into it doesn't reach prod. Pattern confirmed 2026-05-05: cas-7bcf PR #915 went to stale `epic/onboarding-credit-leak-fix-...-cas-e2ba` instead of main; supervisor had to ship a separate PR #916 to main. Correct pattern: `worker/cas-XXXX` → `main` (or whatever the current integration branch is).
